newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish minister under pressure over ERM link.
newsitem.headline: Finnish minister under pressure over ERM link.

text.p: A shift towards the opposition in European Parliament elections, plus a legal technicality, are raising pressure on Finland's second finance minister, Arja Alho, who is caught in a row about the markka's link to ERM.

Social Democrat Alho on television on Tuesday said she was "beginning to have had enough" after a controversy fueled last week when an opposition Centre Party member of parliament accused her of breaking the law during talks to peg the currency within the EU Exchange Rate Mechanism.

Finland's Chancellor of Justice, who monitors the legality of government actions, is investigating the claim that Alho gave secret information to the EU counterparty ahead of negotiations to link the markka to the ERM on October 12.
Alho said on Tuesday she had confirmed the negotiating range ahead of the talks, in contact with EU commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy and Irish Finance Minister Ruari Quinn.

This may be against the letter of Finland's Money Act. It forbids giving out information about the markka's exchange rate when it is linked to any currency system until the government has made a final decision.

Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen has repeatedly defended Alho, saying she acted in line with instructions and totally in the country's interest. He has also said EU representatives described the peg as "a perfect operation".

But SDP politicians say Alho does not have strong support among her colleagues, and with the government losing ground to the opposition in the October 20 Europoll, pressure is mounting to find a scapegoat.
The Centre Party won 24.4 percent of the vote, against 21.5 percent for the Social Democrats who head the coalition and who ushered the markka into the mechanism a week before the poll.
Even if Alho were cleared of all suspicion she may still have to go, party sources said on Wednesday. Media commentators have even said Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is now Alho's only supporter.
"The pressures would ease but not go away," one SDP source said.
